Age: 4 years
Sex: male
Race/ethnicity: unspecified
Site of care: office

The patient's family immigrated to the United States several months ago, and they have brought him for evaluation due to extreme fatigue and occasional syncope.  His mother says the patient has had episodes of agitation and tachypnea since birth; these episodes have progressively worsened to the point that he sometimes loses consciousness.  Cardiac examination shows a harsh systolic ejection murmur heard over the left sternal border.  Oxygen saturation is 82% while supine and 91% while squatting.  The patient's condition is most likely due to which of the following disruptions of fetal development?​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​​​​​​​​‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​

explanation:
This young boy with intermittent episodes of agitation, tachypnea, and syncope, as well as a harsh systolic murmur and hypoxemia that improves with squatting, most likely has tetralogy of Fallot (ToF).  ToF consists of 4 abnormalities that all result from anterior and cephalad deviation of the infundibular septum during fetal development.

The most important abnormalities in ToF are right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) obstruction and large ventricular septal defect (VSD); the degree of RVOT obstruction is the major determinant of symptoms.  When RVOT obstruction is severe, blood is forced to bypass the lungs and shunt right-to-left through the large VSD, causing hypoxemia and cyanosis.

Because some degree of RVOT obstruction is fixed and some degree is dynamic, patients often experience periodic episodes of worsening hypoxemia (ie, tet episodes) that may be accompanied by syncope.  These episodes are often precipitated by feeding or crying, which can shift the infundibular septum and cause a dynamic increase in RVOT obstruction.  Squatting, or the assumption of a knee-to-chest position, can often improve a tet episode (ie, improve hypoxemia) by increasing systemic afterload to reduce right-to-left shunting through the VSD.

(Choice A)  Absent spiraling of the conotruncal septum results in transposition of the great arteries (TGA).  TGA involves parallel systemic and pulmonary circulations; it typically does not cause a murmur and presents with persistent cyanosis at birth.

(Choice C)  Arrested growth of the septum secundum results in a secundum atrial septal defect (ASD).  An isolated ASD is usually asymptomatic until adulthood; cyanosis/hypoxemia is rare and occurs only if Eisenmenger syndrome develops over many years.

(Choice D)  Circumferential wall thickening of the preductal aorta describes coarctation of the aorta (CoA).  Severe CoA can cause differential cyanosis/hypoxemia in the immediate newborn period but it otherwise does not cause cyanosis/hypoxemia.

(Choice E)  Failed fusion of the superior and inferior endocardial cushions leads to a complete atrioventricular canal defect, which consists of an ASD, VSD, and single atrioventricular valve.  The condition usually presents with heart failure within the first year of life; cyanosis/hypoxemia is not expected unless Eisenmenger syndrome eventually develops.

Educational objective:Tetralogy of Fallot results from anterior and cephalad deviation of the infundibular septum during fetal development.  Patients commonly have episodic cyanosis caused by a dynamic increase in right ventricular outflow tract obstruction that forces right-to-left shunting through the large ventricular septal defect.  Squatting can improve the cyanosis by increasing systemic afterload to reduce right-to-left shunting.​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​​​​​​​​‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​
